title: The Ottomans rise
hookLine: a small Anatolian state becomes an empire

lines: A SMALL STATE ON THE EDGE.
cards: When the Seljuk sultans of Anatolia weakened, their land broke into small principalities, each with its own chief, its own few towns, its own horsemen.
On the far northwest edge, facing the Byzantine Empire, sat a small one. A frontier strip of hills and pasture. Its leader was a man named Osman.
Seen from the old Seljuk city of Konya, he was one frontier chief among several. And yet his name would one day be carried by a great empire. In English, Osman's people became the Ottomans.

teach.b: Later Ottoman chroniclers tell a story about Osman's beginnings. It's a story people tell, not a record. Osman is staying in the house of a holy man, a sheikh.
He falls asleep and dreams that a moon rises from the sheikh's chest and settles into his own.

teach.h: A TREE WHOSE SHADE COVERS CITIES.
teach.b: Then a tree grows from him, its branches spreading until their shade covers mountains, rivers and cities.
When he wakes, the sheikh reads the dream as a promise for his descendants, and gives Osman his daughter in marriage.
Whatever happened in that house, the story tells you how the dynasty wanted to be remembered: blessed by a man of God, from a seed that grew. The real growth was slower and more ordinary.

teach.h: ONE TOWN AT A TIME: BURSA.
teach.b: Osman and his son Orhan took towns one at a time from the Byzantines. Orhan made Bursa their city, and father and son are buried there. They drew in warriors, scholars, Sufi brotherhoods and Christian villagers alike.
One town, then a region, then a crossing into Europe. A small frontier state became an empire. The Qur'an has a line about small things that matter.
In Pickthall's translation: "And whoso doeth good an atom's weight will see it then."
And a saying of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, in Sahih al-Bukhari, holds that the deeds God loves best are those done steadily, even if they are small.
An empire is not a good deed, and the Ottomans did both good and harm. But the shape of the story is worth keeping: a seed, a dream, and a lot of patient steps.

how: Turkish Muslims visit the tombs of Osman and Orhan in Bursa, and the story of Osman's dream is still told as the founding legend of the Ottoman dynasty.

games.q: you're Osman, chief of a small frontier state. bigger neighbors surround you. what's your path to growing?
o: one great battle to take everything at once.
one town at a time, drawing many kinds of people in.
games.why: Osman and Orhan grew town by town, gathering warriors, scholars, Sufis and Christian villagers, until the frontier state became an empire.

practice: Bring to mind one thing in your life that started small: a friendship that began with one conversation, a skill that began with one clumsy try, a habit of prayer or kindness that began on an ordinary day. Hold it for a while.
Then think of one small seed you could plant, so small it feels almost silly, and if you pray, ask for it to grow.

wordCard.voice: Osman. The frontier chief whose small state in Anatolia grew one town at a time into the Ottoman empire. Today's word.
